hints: Focus on what the yellow precipitate with alkaline iodine really tells you, it only happens with a very specific small group in the alcohol.
Check each alcohol for a $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ unit, this immediately rules out two of the four structures.
Now think about oxidation, only a primary $\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$ group can be oxidised to an aldehyde that turns Fehling's red-brown, secondary groups only give ketones.
walkthrough:
**Decode the iodoform test**

Y gives a yellow precipitate with alkaline aqueous iodine. This is the tri-iodomethane (iodoform) test, positive only for molecules containing $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ or $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$.

Test rule:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}- \xrightarrow{\text{I}_2 / \text{NaOH}} \text{CHI}_3 \text{(yellow ppt)}$$

**Decode the Fehling's test**

Z gives a red-brown precipitate with Fehling's solution. That means Z must be an aldehyde, $\text{RCHO}$, because ketones do not react.

Test rule:
$$\text{RCHO} + \text{Fehling's (blue)} \rightarrow \text{Cu}_2\text{O} \text{(red-brown ppt)}$$

**Link Z back to Y by oxidation**

Y is an alcohol oxidised to make Z. To make an aldehyde, Y must contain a primary alcohol group, $\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$, which oxidises first to $\text{-CHO}$.

Oxidation link:
$$\text{R-CH}_2\text{OH} \xrightarrow{[O]} \text{R-CHO} \xrightarrow{[O]} \text{R-COOH}$$

**Apply both clues to find Y**

So Y needs BOTH features at once: a $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ group for the iodoform test, and a separate $\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$ group to be oxidised to an aldehyde for Fehling's.

Only $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_2\text{OH}$ has both, oxidation of its primary end gives $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH(CH}_3\text{)CHO}$, a hydroxy-aldehyde that is Fehling's positive.

options.A: Contains $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ so it gives yellow $\text{CHI}_3$ with $\text{I}_2/\text{NaOH}$. It also contains a primary $\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$ which on controlled oxidation gives the aldehyde $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH(CH}_3\text{)CHO}$. This aldehyde gives the red-brown $\text{Cu}_2\text{O}$ precipitate with Fehling's. Both conditions are satisfied.
options.B: Structure is $\text{CH}_3\text{C(OH)(CH}_3\text{)CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$. It has a tertiary alcohol and a primary alcohol but no $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ group, so the iodoform test is negative. The tertiary $\text{-OH}$ also resists oxidation. A common trap is to see $\text{CH}_3\text{-C}$ and think it is iodoform positive.
options.C: Structure is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$ (pentane-2,4-diol). It does contain $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ so the iodoform test is positive, but both $\text{-OH}$ groups are secondary. Oxidation can only give hydroxy-ketones and diketones, never an aldehyde, so no product gives a positive Fehling's test.
options.D: Structure is $\text{CH}_2\text{(OH)CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. Its secondary alcohol is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)}-$, not $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$, so the iodoform test is negative. Although its primary $\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$ could oxidise to an aldehyde that is Fehling's positive, it fails the first test, so it cannot be Y.
